# 1 Clement Chapter 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 17 continues the examples of humility, now drawn from the prophets and OT saints. The phrase "those who went about in goatskins and sheepskins" (v.1) is an echo of Hebrews 11:37, suggesting either that Clement knows Hebrews or both draw on a common tradition.

The three humility-statements — Abraham's "dust and ashes" (Gen 18:27), Job's "no man is clean" (Job 14:4-5), and Moses's "Who am I?" (Exod 3:10-11) — form a crescendo: from the patriarch to the sufferer to the lawgiver, all confess their unworthiness before God.

The "vapor from the cauldron" citation (v.6) has no exact parallel in the LXX; it may be from the lost expansion of Numbers 11 or a catechetical variant.

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** Let us also be imitators of those who went about in goatskins and sheepskins, heralding the coming of Christ — I mean Elijah and Elisha and Ezekiel among the prophets, and likewise those who have received attestation.

**17:2** Abraham received great attestation and was called "Friend of God"; and yet, gazing on the glory of God with humility of mind, he said: "I am but dust and ashes." [Gen 18:27]

**17:3** Concerning Job also it is written: "Job was righteous and blameless, true and God-fearing, one who kept himself from every evil thing." [Job 1:1, 8 LXX]

**17:4** Yet he, passing judgment on himself, says: "No man is clean from defilement, not even if his life be but a single day." [Job 14:4-5 LXX]

**17:5** Moses was called "faithful in all his house," and through his ministry God judged Egypt with plagues and torments. Yet even he, though glorified, uttered no word of arrogance; but when the oracle was given to him from the burning bush, he said: "Who am I, that you should send me? I am weak in speech and slow of tongue." [Num 12:7; Exod 3:10-11; 4:10 LXX]

**17:6** And again he says: "I am vapor from a pot." [variant citation]

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
